approved_deviations.subject: Key scoring compares the input's raw root string against sharp candidate names, so a flat-root input scores 0:2 where the sharp spelling scores 2:2

approved_deviations.reason: Only the score field differs, membership and order are identical, and no client can reach the case: the URL codec rejects non-sharp roots and after CORE-D06 every wire surface is sharp-only

approved_deviations.subject: Modal grouping drops any group that is not a perfect seven-mode set, so a perfect match can leave the panel empty
approved_deviations.baseline_output: 0 rows for the first two (a perfect C major shows nothing), the surviving pentatonic row for the third, and 7 of 9 perfect suggestions for the fourth (G major and E minor vanish)
approved_deviations.native_output: a perfect suggestion is never dropped: the incomplete modal group is shown as its own row and its members are shown, so nothing that fits perfectly is hidden
approved_deviations.reason: Showing less than exists is fidelity; showing nothing while a perfect match exists is a defect the user chose not to inherit. The row order itself is deterministic (the note-set key term order) and is ported verbatim, so only the drop deviates
